def: Swelling of the conjunctiva that makes it bulge like a clear blister over the eye. Seen in allergy, orbital cellulitis, thyroid eye disease and cavernous sinus thrombosis.
A toxic metabolite of ifosfamide that causes neurotoxicity and may contribute to kidney damage. Methylene blue is used for treatment.
Resembling cartilage. Chondroid matrix on imaging or histology, such as ring-and-arc calcifications, suggests a cartilage-forming tumor like chondrosarcoma.
Breakdown and loss of articular cartilage, which can complicate slipped capital femoral epiphysis or surgical pinning of the hip.
Describes involuntary movements combining quick, jerky motions (chorea) with slow, writhing ones (athetosis), as in some cerebral palsy and kernicterus.
Relating to scarring. Cicatricial trachoma causes eyelid scarring and inward turning of lashes, leading to corneal damage.
A tree bark that is the natural source of quinine and quinidine.
Toxicity from quinine or quinidine, causing tinnitus, headache, dizziness, blurred vision and nausea.
Sideways curvature of a finger, most often the fifth finger bending toward the fourth. A feature of Down syndrome.
Congenital shortening or absence of the radius, causing the hand to angle toward the thumb side. Seen with Fanconi anemia, TAR syndrome and VACTERL.
A bumpy, paved-stone appearance of a mucosal surface. Seen in Crohn disease of the intestine and in allergic rhinitis of the nose.
Pain in the tailbone (coccyx), usually after a fall or prolonged sitting. Neurologic exam is normal.
Inheritance in which both alleles of a gene are fully expressed in the heterozygote, as in AB blood type.
The mesothelium lining the embryonic body cavity; ovarian surface epithelial tumors (serous, mucinous) are derived from it.
The age at first sexual intercourse. Early coitarche is a risk factor for HPV infection and cervical cancer.
A benign skin nodule of excess collagen. Multiple collagenomas, with facial angiofibromas, occur in MEN1.
A stool test for colorectal cancer screening that detects altered DNA markers and hidden blood. Positive results require colonoscopy.
Surgery that closes off the vagina to treat pelvic organ prolapse in older women who are no longer sexually active.
A high-grade type of ductal carcinoma in situ (DCIS) in the breast with central necrosis in the ducts, which often calcifies on mammography.
Filling memory gaps with fabricated but believable stories, without intent to deceive. Characteristic of Korsakoff syndrome.
A fungal stalk bearing spore-producing cells. Aspergillus forms a characteristic fruiting body with conidia radiating from a swollen head.
A ring of six connexin proteins forming one half of a gap junction channel, allowing small molecules and ions to pass between adjacent cells.
Tiny freshwater crustaceans (water fleas) that host the larvae of Dracunculus medinensis (guinea worm). People get infected by drinking contaminated water.
Involuntary utterance of obscene or socially inappropriate words, seen in a minority of Tourette syndrome patients.
An upper arm muscle that flexes and adducts the arm at the shoulder, innervated by the musculocutaneous nerve.
Surgical removal of all or part of a vocal cord, used for early glottic cancer.
A small cartilage at the tip of each arytenoid in the larynx, derived from pharyngeal arches 4 and 6.
Screening for cervical cancer with both a Pap smear and HPV testing at once. Not recommended before age 30 because HPV is common and usually clears in young women.
A thin muscle layer around the spermatic cord that raises the testis. The cremasteric reflex, tested by stroking the inner thigh, is lost in testicular torsion.
A protein (NLRP3) forming an inflammasome that activates IL-1. Gain-of-function mutations cause cryopyrin-associated periodic syndromes such as familial cold autoinflammatory syndrome.
Failure of one or both testes to descend into the scrotum. Raises risk of infertility and testicular cancer.
A protozoan parasite shed as acid-fast oocysts in stool. Causes watery diarrhea, severe and prolonged in AIDS, and spreads through contaminated water.
Methemoglobin bound to cyanide. Nitrites treat cyanide poisoning by creating methemoglobin, which binds cyanide so it is kept away from cytochrome oxidase.
The synthetic form of vitamin B12 used in supplements and injections to treat pernicious anemia and other B12 deficiencies.
A blue tinge to vision, a side effect of sildenafil and other PDE-5 inhibitors through inhibition of PDE-6 in the retina.
A single central eye in the midline of the face, the most severe result of holoprosencephaly.
A potassium binder taken by mouth that traps potassium in the gut to treat hyperkalemia.
The receptor that binds leukotrienes C4, D4 and E4 and causes bronchoconstriction and mucus production in asthma. Blocked by montelukast and zafirlukast.
Surgical creation of a connection between a pancreatic pseudocyst and the stomach to drain it, done for large or symptomatic cysts older than 6 weeks.
Direct inspection of the bladder and urethra with a thin scope passed through the urethra.
A kinase inhibitor of mutant BRAF (V600E), used with trametinib in melanoma.
A teardrop-shaped red blood cell, seen in myelofibrosis, thalassemia and marrow infiltration.
